title: Policy-Based Authorization
description: Policy-based authorization lets you define reusable authorization rules in ASP.NET Core. Policies combine requirements and handlers to enforce complex access rules cleanly.

data.text: Policy-based authorization lets you define access rules as reusable policies. Each policy consists of requirements (what must be true) and handlers (how to evaluate those requirements). This keeps authorization logic out of your controllers.

data.title: Defining a Custom Policy
data.content: Create a minimum age requirement and policy.

terms.definition: A named set of requirements that must be satisfied for authorization to succeed.
A condition that the authorization system checks, represented by a class implementing IAuthorizationRequirement.
A class that evaluates a requirement and calls context.Succeed() or context.Fail().

data.title: Built-In Policies
data.text: ASP.NET Core includes built-in policies like RequireAuthenticatedUser, RequireRole, and RequireClaim. Use custom policies only when built-in ones are not enough.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Policies separate authorization rules from controllers
Requirements define what must be true
data.takeaway: Policy-based authorization is the most maintainable way to enforce complex access rules.

data.title: Exercise: Create a Department Policy
data.description: Require users to belong to a specific department to access an endpoint.
steps: Create a DepartmentRequirement with a DepartmentName property
Create a DepartmentHandler that checks the user's department claim
Register the policy in Program.cs with department name 'HR'
Test with tokens that have and lack the department claim
data.expectedOutcome: Only users with the matching department claim can access the protected endpoint.
